Scottish Assessors Association (SAA)

Reviewed by Oliver Wakefield-Smith, Founder, Digital Signet. Rates read from HMRC, the VOA, the Scottish Government and the OBR.Topic: tax bands
rates verified 13 Nov 2026 · next refresh after the Scottish Budget 2027-28
Direct answer

The Scottish Assessors Association is the body that draws together Scotland's 14 Assessors, who between them band every home in the 32 council areas. Its public portal at saa.gov.uk is where you look up any Scottish council tax band or non-domestic rateable value by postcode, and where you lodge a proposal against a band.28 Your band is a question for the Assessor; your bill, discounts and exemptions are for your council.29

Scotland's 14 Assessors and the councils they cover

Find your council in the right-hand column: that Assessor sets your band and handles your proposal. The list is the SAA's own.46

Ten of the 14 are valuation joint boards shared by two to four councils; Dumfries & Galloway, Fife, Glasgow City and Scottish Borders each have their own Assessor. Assessors without their own website are reached through saa.gov.uk.

Council tax valuation bands (Scotland), A to H

The Assessor places each home in one band on its open market value at 1 April 1991. The band then fixes what share of the council's Band D charge you pay. The values are from the SAA,47 the proportions from the Local Government Finance Act 1992 s.74 as amended from 1 April 2017.48

Scottish council tax bands: 1991 value range and proportion of Band D
Band1991 valueShare of D× D
AUp to £27,000240/3600.67
B£27,001 to £35,000280/3600.78
C£35,001 to £45,000320/3600.89
D£45,001 to £58,000360/3601.00
E£58,001 to £80,000473/3601.31
F£80,001 to £106,000585/3601.63
G£106,001 to £212,000705/3601.96
HOver £212,000882/3602.45

A Band H home pays 2.45 times the Band D charge, and a Band A home two thirds of it. Proposed bands I and J are on the Scottish council tax bands page.

What the SAA is

The SAA was instituted in 1975, at the time of local government reorganisation, as a voluntary body that brings together all of Scotland's Assessors and Electoral Registration Officers. Each Assessor is responsible, in their own area, for council tax banding, non-domestic (business) rating and the electoral register. The Association exists to share knowledge and keep practice consistent across those areas; it is the Assessors, not the Association, who make the individual banding decisions.28

How to check a council tax band on saa.gov.uk

The Scottish Assessors' Portal gives free public access to the Valuation Lists (council tax bands) and Valuation Rolls (rateable values) for eligible properties across Scotland. Enter a postcode or address and the portal returns the band the Assessor has assigned. If you disagree with a band you can make a proposal through the same site; strict time limits apply, so check the grounds and deadline before you start.29

Who to contact

  • Your band, or a proposal to change it: the Assessor for your council (table above), through saa.gov.uk.
  • Your bill, discounts, exemptions, Council Tax Reduction, arrears or change of address: your local council, not the Assessor.29
